****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****[[2026 United States naval blockade of Iran]]
******The [[United States Central Command]] (CENTCOM) says that [[United States Armed Forces|American forces]] have redirected two commercial vessels since the blockade resumed. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/us-says-2-commercial-vessels-redirected-since-iran-naval-blockade-resumed/3999159 (AA)]

An 18 second video confirms that a [[List of active United States military aircraft|U.S. aircraft]] disabled the vessel. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/us-israel-iran-war/us-says-it-disabled-oil-tanker-trying-to-breach-iran-naval-blockade/3999657 (AA)] [https://www.stripes.com/theaters/middle_east/2026-07-15/us-forces-disable-vessel-arabian-gulf-22276200.html (''Stars and Stripes'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[United Kingdom–European Union relations]]
**[[Effect of Brexit on Gibraltar]]
***The [[United Kingdom]] and the [[European Union]] remove [[Gibraltar–Spain border|the land-border]] fence between [[Gibraltar]] and [[Spain]] under a post-[[Brexit]] treaty, allowing [[Freedom of movement|free movement]] while introducing joint British-Spanish [[Border control|checks]] at [[Gibraltar International Airport|Gibraltar's airport]] and [[Port of Gibraltar|port]]. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-gibraltar-uk-brexit-9113dd58dc8220826038022e84e3b662 (AP)]
*[[Afghanistan and the United Nations]]

[https://www.arabnews.com/node/2651083/amp (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[Papua New Guinea–Taiwan relations]]
**[[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Papua New Guinea)|Papuan foreign minister]] [[Justin Tkatchenko]] announces the immediate closure of [[Taiwan]]'s [[Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office|representative office]] in [[Port Moresby]], citing [[Papua New Guinea]]'s adherence to the [[One China]] policy, while saying the decision does not affect contracts between Taiwan's [[CPC Corporation]] and [[natural gas in Papua New Guinea]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/china-says-papua-new-guinea-has-closed-taiwans-office-in-the-country (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Bhutanese refugees scam]]
**A [[District Courts of Nepal|district court]] in [[Kathmandu District|Kathmandu]], [[Nepal]], sentences former [[Deputy Prime Minister of Nepal|deputy prime minister]] [[Top Bahadur Rayamajhi]] to four years in prison and former [[Ministry of Home Affairs (Nepal)|home minister]] [[Bal Krishna Khand]] to two years for roles in [[Forgery|forging]] documents for a fraudulent [[Bhutanese refugees|Bhutanese refugee]] resettlement scheme. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nepal-court-jails-2-former-ministers-14-others-over-refugee-scam-2026-07-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Cannabis in Kenya]]
**[[Kenya]]'s [[High Court (Kenya)|High Court]] rejects a [[Rastafari in Africa|Rastafarian]] petition seeking a [[religious exemption]] from [[cannabis laws]], ruling that the group does not show the laws violate [[religious freedom]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/kenya-high-court-marijuana-legalisation-rastafarian-religious-rights-not-essential-kenyan-court-denies-rastafarians-right-to-smoke-weed-11775102 (AFP via NDTV)]
*[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict (2022–present)|Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] establishes a council composed of mostly international [[war crime]]s lawyers to advise state institutions seeking accountability and [[Reparations (transitional justice)|reparations]] for victims of violence in the country's east. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-forms-new-council-push-war-crimes-justice-2026-07-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Detention of Craig and Lindsay Foreman]]
**The family of British national Craig Foreman says an [[Judicial system of the Islamic Republic of Iran|Iranian court]] has added two years to his 10-year [[espionage]] prison sentence for speaking to the media, as he and his wife Lindsay continue a [[hunger strike]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iran-uk-lindsay-craig-foreman-prison-sentence-hunger-strike-son-worried/ (CBS News)]
*[[Morocco|Moroccan]] prosecutors release [[Mass media in Morocco|journalist]] [[Ali Lmrabet]] after questioning him over [[Internet in Morocco|online posts]] allegedly [[defaming]] unnamed individuals and institutions, while the criminal investigation continues. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/morocco-releases-dissident-journalist-ali-lmrabet-2026-07-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that American citizen Dena Karari has been released from Iran after being [[List of foreign nationals detained in Iran|detained]] on espionage charges since 2024. Her lawyer, [[Jared Genser]], also confirmed her release. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/15/trump-iran-detained-citizen-released (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/trump-announces-release-us-citizen-held-iran-2024-dena-karari-rcna587764 (NBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Astronomers directly image the [[exoplanet]] [[Beta Pictoris d]] next to [[Beta Pictoris|its star]], located 63 light-years away, using [[NASA]]'s [[James Webb Space Telescope]] and [[European Southern Observatory]]'s [[Very Large Telescope]]. It is also reported to be fainter than its sibling [[Beta Pictoris b]]. The discovery is published in the ''[[The Astrophysical Journal]]''. [https://abcnews.com/amp/Technology/wireStory/faint-new-planet-revealed-young-star-after-decade-134776523 (ABC News)] [https://www.space.com/astronomy/exoplanets/found-you-astronomers-spot-faintest-exoplanet-ever-seen-from-earth-after-a-decade-of-hide-and-seek (Space.com)]

[https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/07/16/world/amazon-to-launch-south-africa-satellite-internet-as-starlink-awaits-license/2385395 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
